tasks.title: Lane fixture and serial baseline: a sandbox repo with 9 tasks (6 independent, 3 chained by waits_on, 3 editing one shared function), each with a verify command. Serial drive's wall-clock, tasks done, verify pass rate, tokens per task and conflicts are the bar every later step must beat

Load control so lanes do not saturate the machine: a verify semaphore (one full suite at a time), nice/taskpolicy for sessions and verify, process-group kill on verify timeout, a vitest maxWorkers cap (drive-load note 01M3PCDC, fixes 1-5)
Ready frontier: readyTasks honours waits_on (queuedTasks ignores it today, drive-queue.ts:42); `sofar next --ready`; serial drive takes the ready head
Record-root override: a lane session writes the main checkout's .sofar, never its worktree's stale committed copy; lanes never commit .sofar

`sofar drive --lanes N`: a persistent lane worktree pool (deps installed once), tasks as branches, lanes recorded on run_started. `--lanes 1` stays byte-identical to today's run (session-driver D6 holds there)

Coordinator: one process assigns ready tasks to free lanes and records each assignment, so the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task. Budgets (--cost-cap, --max-sessions) count across lanes; a rate-limited lane parks instead of stalling

Serial merge queue: rebase a passing task branch onto the run base, re-verify when the base moved, fast-forward. A conflict becomes a merge handoff to the lane's next session. Affected-tests verify per merge, full suite per batch

Measure local lanes against serial on the 1.1 fixture. Keep only if wall-clock falls ≥40%, duplicate work is 0, tasks done and verify pass rate are no lower, merge-conflict reopens ≤10% and tokens per task rise ≤5%

Region leases at PreToolUse: an Edit's old_string maps to its markdown section or enclosing symbol, else the whole file. An overlap with another lane stops the edit with a reason; the session works elsewhere or parks (WIP commit, write-back, leases released). Older task wins, so no deadlock; union-merge files never lease. NEEDS the operator's ruling on r4-fixes D17 (deny only on an explicit-forbid rule) for driven lanes

Footprint prediction and conflict-aware scheduling: task `touches`, the record's mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. A free lane takes the first ready task that misses every live lease and footprint, else idles; skipped tasks age up

Context packets, deterministic and one line each: lease notice (who holds what, for which task), change brief on merge (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet (own write-back, WIP sha, the brief it waited for)
Measure conflict-aware lanes against naive lanes: merge-conflict rework sessions, parks, lanes busy, wall-clock. Keep each piece only if it improves on 2.5

Cloud launch and readback without a TTY: `claude --cloud` refuses a non-TTY (r4-fixes M24). Verify a scriptable launch (routines via API call, or a pty), a branch per task, results back through pushed branches (needs the Claude GitHub App on the repo), and session end detected from the branch's record

Cloud lane adapter: a lane is a cloud session on its task branch. The local coordinator polls and fetches, verifies locally, merges through the queue, and `--resume` re-attaches after the laptop sleeps (the record is the queue)
Conflicts in cloud lanes: no edit-time leases (a cloud VM cannot read the local lease store), so scheduling by footprint plus the merge queue. Measure conflict rework against local lanes
Measure cloud lanes against local lanes: wall-clock, cost per task, tasks finished with the laptop closed, verify pass rate
